---
title: "GABM Logistic Regression"
author: "Ross"
date: "2025-04-25"
output: html_document
---

```{r}
#####################################################################
# table1_models.R  – Replicates the four Table-1 regressions in R
# Raw prevalence version • Column names adapted: slight_cough → SlightCough
#####################################################################

# 1.  Packages -------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)     # fast read & write
library(dplyr)          # data wrangling
library(fixest)         # fixed-effects logit (feglm)
library(lme4)           # random-effects logit (glmer)
library(broom)          # tidy model outputs
library(performance)    # BIC & pseudo-R²
library(modelsummary)   # convenient table export

# 2.  Import the CSV -------------------------------------------------
df <- fread("AllRuns_Indiv_Data_for_logistic_regression.csv")

# 3.  Unique agent id = run number + name ----------------------------
df <- df %>%
  mutate(agent_key = paste0(`Run Number`, "_", name),
         id        = as.integer(factor(agent_key)))   # numeric id like Stata’s encode

# 4.  Stata-friendly names ------------------------------------------
df <- df %>%
  rename(time            = `Time Step`,
         StayHome        = Response,
         SlightCough     = slight_cough,
         FeverCough      = cough_and_fever,
         CaseFeedback    = `Daily New Cases Day 4`,
         extraversion    = Extraversion,
         agreeableness   = Agreeableness,
         conscientiousness = Conscientiousness,
         emotional_stability = `Emotional Stability`,
         intellect       = `Openness to Experience`)

# 5.  Quadratic term (raw^2) ----------------------------------------
df <- df %>% mutate(CaseFeedback2 = CaseFeedback^2)
# If CaseFeedback is a raw count and you need to divide by 1000, do it here:
# df <- df %>% mutate(CaseFeedback   = CaseFeedback/1000,
#                     CaseFeedback2 = CaseFeedback^2)

# 6.  Panel structure helper ----------------------------------------
# fixest will absorb `id` as the fixed effect; no explicit xtset needed.
# If you ever want plm-style pdata.frame:
# df <- pdata.frame(df, index = c("id", "time"))

# 7.  Regression 1 (FE): Slight + Fever -----------------------------
FE1 <- feglm(StayHome ~ SlightCough + FeverCough | id,
             data = df, family = "logit")

# 8.  Regression 2 (FE): add CaseFeedback ---------------------------
FE2 <- feglm(StayHome ~ SlightCough + FeverCough + CaseFeedback | id,
             data = df, family = "logit")

# 9.  Regression 3 (FE): add CaseFeedback² --------------------------
FE3 <- feglm(StayHome ~ SlightCough + FeverCough +
                           CaseFeedback + CaseFeedback2 | id,
             data = df, family = "logit")

# 10. Regression 4 (RE): traits + age + gender ----------------------
RE4 <- glmer(StayHome ~ SlightCough + FeverCough +
                           CaseFeedback + CaseFeedback2 +
                           agreeableness + conscientiousness + extraversion +
                           emotional_stability + intellect +
                           age + gender + (1 | id),
             data = df, family = binomial)

# 11.  Collect coefficients & fit stats -----------------------------
models <- list(FE1 = FE1, FE2 = FE2, FE3 = FE3, RE4 = RE4)

# Helper to pull BIC & McFadden pseudo-R²
fit_stats <- lapply(models, function(m) {
  data.frame(LogLik    = logLik(m),
             BIC       = BIC(m),
             Pseudo_R2 = r2_nakagawa(m)$R2)   # McFadden for feglm, Nakagawa for glmer
}) |> bind_rows(.id = "model")

# 12.  Export --------------------------------------------------------
modelsummary(models,
             statistic  = "({std.error})",
             fmt        = 4,
             gof_omit   = "AIC|RMSE|IC|Deviance",
             add_rows   = list(
               LogLik     = round(fit_stats$LogLik, 1),
               BIC        = round(fit_stats$BIC, 1),
               Pseudo_R2  = round(fit_stats$Pseudo_R2, 3)),
             output     = "table1_coeffs.csv")

# Done!  The CSV now mirrors your Stata estout (coef | se | LogLik | BIC | Pseudo_R2)

```
```{r}
pkgs <- c("data.table", "dplyr", "fixest", "lme4",
          "broom", "performance", "modelsummary")
lapply(pkgs, library, character.only = TRUE)
```
```{r}
# ------------------- INSTALL NEEDED PACKAGES -------------------
pkgs <- c("data.table", "dplyr", "fixest", "lme4",
          "broom", "performance", "modelsummary")

# add a default CRAN mirror so it won't keep asking
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

# install everything that isn't already present
install.packages(setdiff(pkgs, rownames(installed.packages())),
                 dependencies = TRUE)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------

```
